text:
Carla (Customer): Hey, since yesterday's rollout our assistant started dropping the last sentence of its answers and sometimes hallucinating an extra attribution line. Example: it used to answer 'Use X to connect' and now returns 'Use X to connect. Source: unknown' — this is production traffic, big customer impact.
Mira (Support): sorry to hear that, can you paste a minimal repro payload you used?
Carla (Customer): sure, here's an anonymized call we made: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "messages": [{"role":"system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."}, {"role":"user", "content": "How to configure SSO for AcmeCorp?"}]
}
```
Carla (Customer): note we didn't change prompt templates on our side. This started right after your 11:00UTC deploy.
deploy-bot: Deployment completed: release/redwood-chat-1@v2.4.7 (started 2026-03-01T10:57:00Z, finished 2026-03-01T11:02:12Z)
Mira (Support): thanks, filing a priority escalation to infra + ML. tagging Samir.
Mira (Support): quick Q — did you receive any HTTP 5xx or errors, or just degraded content?
Carla (Customer): no errors, 200 OK. Latency similar. Only content differences.
Samir (ML Eng): looking. any chance this correlates with the tokenizer bump we rolled earlier today? I remember a tokenizer patch landed in the v2.4.7 release.
Jonah (Oncall): I'm pulling the release notes/commit list. I see commit 3f9b2a7 updated tokenizer package from 1.4.2 -> 1.5.0 and also changed chat template glue behavior (removed trailing space between system and user tokenization).
Samir (ML Eng): that trailing-space change could change token boundaries for system message + first user tokens; for some prompts that can shift generation distribution.
Mira (Support): Carla, can you test a variant where you set system message to include an extra explicit newline at end? e.g., "You are a helpful assistant.\n" — that might restore previous tokenization alignment as a temporary workaround.
Carla (Customer): tried adding newline, seems closer — the stray attribution line gone on two quick samples.
Samir (ML Eng): good signal. I'm going to reproduce locally with your payload and a diff between tokenizer 1.4.2 and 1.5.0.
Samir (ML Eng): repro steps I'm running:
```
# install two tokenizer versions in venv
pip install tokenizer==1.4.2 -q
python -c "from tokenizer import encode; print(encode('You are a helpful assistant. How to configure SSO for AcmeCorp?'))"
# then repeat with 1.5.0
```
Samir (ML Eng): early results: 1.5.0 gives token split that inserts an extra token boundary before 'How' so the prefix KV cache alignment shifts by one token. That changes the attention context slightly — downstream LM logits differ.
Samir (ML Eng): root cause hypothesis: tokenizer update included a normalization tweak that removed a nonvisible spacer between system and user concatenation in our chat builder. The rollout switched the canonical concatenation string from '\n' to '' (empty) for optimization.
Mira (Support): can we hotfix by pinning tokenizer to 1.4.2 for the hosted service until we have a proper regression fix?
Jonah (Oncall): yes, we can roll back tokenizer bump for the model pool. I'm creating a rollback change: RB-3289. ETA ~30m to revert and warm caches.
Carla (Customer): would appreciate that. Any way to avoid me changing all my templates? We want consistency from your side.
Samir (ML Eng): long-term fix options: 1) revert the tokenizer normalization change, 2) change chat builder to inject explicit separator token ("\n") always between messages, 3) add a regression test for canonical tokenization across template versions. We'll do (2) + (3) and consider (1) if needed.
Mira (Support): I'll keep you updated, Carla. Rolling this to P0.
deploy-bot: Change request created: RB-3289 (rollback tokenizer to 1.4.2) by Jonah.
Jonah (Oncall): RB applied to canary (10%) first. Monitoring logs.
Samir (ML Eng): repro script for internal QA (paste to run): ```bash
# reproduce API call locally
python reproduce_chat.py --model redwood-chat-1 --system "You are a helpful assistant." --user "How to configure SSO for AcmeCorp?" --tokenizer 1.5.0
# reproduce with old tokenizer
python reproduce_chat.py --tokenizer 1.4.2
```
Samir (ML Eng): QA: compare tokenized lengths and top-3 predictions after prefix. If they diverge, mark as regression.
Mira (Support): Carla — once canary rollback reaches 100% we'll confirm with you and then close. For now, as a short-term workaround add a trailing newline to your system message; that should avoid token alignment shifts.
Carla (Customer): thanks, trying now. I'll ping once confirmed. Appreciate the fast triage. :pray:
Samir (ML Eng): note for postmortem: we should avoid silent tokenizer normalization changes without a cross-team signal — small whitespace changes can be high-impact. Adding token-level regression tests to the release checklist.
Mira (Support): logged follow-up action: PM-4412 add tokenizer compat tests and add an alert when a tokenizer bump changes token counts for canonical templates.
Carla (Customer): confirmed after adding newline sample: behavior restored for our workflow. Will wait for rollback to be completed so we can remove our temporary change.
Jonah (Oncall): RB-3289 completed: rolled back tokenizer to 1.4.2 cluster-wide at 11:28UTC. Monitoring shows no new regressions.
Mira (Support): marking thread as underway — will update when we have postmortem and stable release plan.
Carla (Customer): thanks all, will keep monitoring on our side and will reopen if anything else pops up.
